clue.text: Stems from fundamental Christians twice ignoring extreme elements

indicators.note: the outer letters are dropped from each end, and then the new outer letters are dropped again

parts.note: evangelicals are Christians stressing scripture and conversion, often fundamentalist

explanation.surface: Something stems from fundamentalist Christians who keep ignoring the extremists in their ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing E and S, then V and L, from EVANGELICALS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is a plant whose stalks are candied and used to decorate cakes, so it names edible stalks.

clue.text: Alarm about European request

indicators.note: the word for alarm goes round, about, the European letter

parts.note: to alarm or dismay someone is to appal them

explanation.surface: An alarmist plea concerning some European matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest request or plea is an appeal, as in a charity appeal.

clue.text: Vigorous enjoyment in ring after bit of wind

indicators.note: the ring letter is placed after the burst of wind

parts.note: a gust is a brief burst of wind
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Someone relishes life in a boxing ring after a breath of air.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty relish or zest in doing something.

clue.text: Vulgar men do wild acts

indicators.note: the words act upon themselves, performing a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A sneer at the coarse antics of men behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters; 'acts' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-minded means coarse or base in outlook, a close synonym of vulgar.

clue.text: State police can cut crimes

indicators.note: to police is to control and order, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A headline: the state police force is able to reduce crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State police' reads as one phrase, but 'State' is the definition and 'police' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A circumstance is a condition or state of affairs, as in reduced circumstances.

clue.text: Minor finally clothed in fountain in Brussels?

indicators.note: the chosen letter is wrapped inside the word for a fountain

parts.note: a spout is a jet of water like a fountain

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word Minor is used

explanation.surface: Evokes Manneken Pis, the little boy statue-fountain in Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the phrase: the answer is the vegetable that comes after 'Brussels'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brussels sprout is the small cabbage-like vegetable, so the word fits the phrase's gap.

clue.text: Devout Liberal has company ejected

indicators.note: the company abbreviation is thrown out of the word for plentiful

parts.note: liberal in the sense of generous or plentiful, as a liberal helping, means copious

explanation.surface: A devout Liberal politician has had his firm thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' with its capital invites L for the party; it is really an adjective meaning plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Devout and pious are synonyms for deeply religious.

clue.text: Boycott bears up after duck, and is tolerable, in the end

indicators.note: the reversed word comes after the duck letter

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to bear is to carry or convey, as one carts goods

indicators.note: only the final letter of tolerable is taken

explanation.surface: A cricketer named Boycott tolerates a duck: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott someone is to shun or exclude them, the same as to ostracise.

clue.text: Filled cases of tequila, primarily, with skill to get permits

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of tequila is used

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
lets is a synonym of permits or allows

explanation.surface: Containers of tequila, mainly, handled with skill to obtain licences.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartlets are small pastry shells holding a filling, hence filled cases.

clue.text: Pressure fool's wife or daughter to provide access code

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
an ass is a fool; the possessive ending is just surface
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogy

explanation.surface: Someone leans on the fool's spouse or daughter to hand over the login.
explanation.definitionFit: A password is the secret code that grants entry or access.

clue.text: Bill Gates' Centre cracks problem

indicators.note: the central letter breaks into the word for a problem

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling problem

indicators.note: the centre of the name Gates is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Bill Gates, the Microsoft founder, solves a problem at his centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill Gates' reads as a name, but Bill is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice stuck up in public, the same as a poster, as in bill-posting.

clue.text: Foreign invaders are taking over area in mountain range

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take on the area letter at their end
foreign means strange or out of place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Foreign invaders are seizing land in some mountainous region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sierra Nevada is a mountain range in Spain and also one in California.

clue.text: Dip in sea, at last, before 10.51

indicators.note: the sea's final letter comes before the number letters
only the last letter of sea is wanted

parts.note: 10 is written like the letters I and O, and 51 in Roman numerals is LI

explanation.surface: A swim in the sea, at the end, shortly before ten to eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: The time 10.51 is read as letters: IO looks like 10, LI is Roman 51.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise often served as a dip with vegetables or chips.

clue.text: Remove hedge at the end of loveless marriage

indicators.note: the word for hedge is placed after the shortened marriage
love is O in tennis, so the word loses its O

parts.note: a marriage is a union
to hedge is to stall or avoid committing oneself

explanation.surface: Someone takes out the hedge at the bottom of the garden when a cold marriage ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To uninstall is to remove software from a computer.

clue.text: Tycoon in Hindu's trial is tainted

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits inside the run of words Hindu's trial is tainted

explanation.surface: A news story: a businessman is caught up in a Hindu's corrupt trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy, powerful businessperson, especially one running factories.

clue.text: Get drunk at home and eat Brie that's gone off

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: food gone off has spoiled, so the letters of eat Brie are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice for a night in: drink and eat the cheese before it spoils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's gone off' turns EATBRIE into EBRIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inebriate is to make or become intoxicated, a formal word for getting drunk.

clue.text: Excitement as I'm entering American state

indicators.note: the letters of I'm go into the word for state

parts.note: a nation is a state or country

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled on crossing into an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation is liveliness or excited vigour, as in an animated debate.

clue.text: Clown court's harbouring new plots

indicators.note: the clown and court together take in and shelter the letter for new

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown
CT is an abbreviation for court, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A circus clown at court hides some fresh schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: To concoct is to devise or cook up a scheme, so it means to plot.

clue.text: Make excessively emotional movie star read broadcast

indicators.note: seeds broadcast are scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A movie star hams it up while reading on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdramatise is to present something with exaggerated emotion or theatricality.

clue.text: Exercise freak swallows a legume

indicators.note: the combined word takes in the letter a

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a nut or freak is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A fitness fanatic gulps down a bean.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is botanically a legume, related to peas and beans, not a true nut.

clue.text: Account of persistent case of lice

parts.note: chronic describes a long-lasting, persistent condition

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A medical record of a persistent lice infestation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical record or narrative account of events.

clue.text: Terrible thing, darkness

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters of thing are mangled

explanation.surface: A shudder at the dark: what a terrible thing it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period of darkness between sunset and sunrise.

clue.text: Ampere is the French word meaning passageway

parts.note: A is the symbol for the ampere, the unit of current
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style entry for a French word meaning a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats or shelves.

clue.text: Relish pertness

definitions.meaning: a relish is a condiment, a tasty accompaniment to food
pertness is cheeky impudence, as in none of your lip

explanation.surface: Two nouns side by side: a tasty dressing and cheeky talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is both a condiment and, informally, cheek or impertinence.

clue.text: Responsibility each Argentinian carries

indicators.note: the words each Argentinian carry the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Every Argentinian bears a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a duty or care entrusted to someone, as in in charge of.

clue.text: One involved in diplomacy to make money, it's rumoured, is reticent

indicators.note: the numeral is set inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is diplomacy, sensitivity in dealing with others
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: rumour is hearsay, so the word for making money is taken as heard

parts.note: to earn is to make money

explanation.surface: A diplomat out to profit is said to be tight-lipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn means habitually silent or reserved, so it fits reticent; 'is' is part of the definition.

clue.text: See ex-Prime Minister in figure-hugging dress

parts.note: S is a dictionary abbreviation for see, as in cross-references
Edward Heath was UK Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: An image of a former PM squeezed into a tight dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; Ted Heath was a British Conservative Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting dress that follows the body's shape.

clue.text: Most feeble exam score of zero?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, sweet FA (nothing) in a test: scoring nothing in an exam

explanation.surface: A sneer at the weakest candidate, who scored nothing in the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all; the second reading splits the answer into that slang and 'in test'.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of faint means weakest or least perceptible, matching most feeble.
